primary_claim: Across 14 frontier models and 3 alignment evals (MASK honesty, APE persuasion, a custom sycophancy eval), meaning-preserving prompt rephrasing produced broadly noisy and inconsistent effects on misalignment scores, with no clear trend supporting either hypothesis that larger models are less affected by prompt variation or that deeper perturbation tiers have larger effects, although hypothetical framing consistently increased sycophancy scores and prompt variation changed misalignment scores more than control-repeat noise in the sycophancy eval.

effect.metric: change in misalignment score under prompt variation vs baseline/control-repeat noise; correlation between ECI and change in sycophancy score under hypothetical framing
effect.value: no clear relationship between model capability (ECI) and prompt-variation sensitivity, nor between perturbation tier and effect size; significant negative correlation between ECI and hypothetical-framing-induced sycophancy increase; in the sycophancy eval, prompt variation exceeds control-repeat noise for almost all models

contradicts_or_qualifies: did not find support for either main hypothesis (larger models less affected by prompt variation; higher-tier perturbations having larger effects), qualifying the expectation that prompt sensitivity scales predictably with model capability or perturbation depth
found basic rigor flaws in several evals listed on Inspect, including missing control conditions, weak theoretical motivation, and results reported to a precision finer than their own uncertainty
stated_future_work: undertake a sensitivity analysis to identify and minimise sources of error unrelated to prompt variation (e.g. LLM-generated variation quality, judge quality, temperature, refusal rates)
revise and develop a more principled taxonomy of prompt variation dimensions, ideally grounded in existing datasets
undertake a grid search across combinations of variations rather than one dimension at a time
apply prompt variation to the system prompt as well as the user prompt
apply prompt variation to multi-turn evaluations
limitations_stated: many models' baseline scores clustered near 0 or 1, risking floor/ceiling effects
substantial variability across evals for the same model, presumably because the evals measure different underlying properties despite being clumped into one score
a very small set of base user prompts (2 for MASK, 2 for APE, 3 for Sycophancy) limits how confidently the findings generalise beyond the specific scenarios tested
the hypothetical-framing/sycophancy finding is a single eval/dimension combination and risks being a cherry-picked result
